name: Carrion Defense Works Scythe CDW-20 'Reaper'
description:
A mounted heavy support weapon that fires 15mm explosive-tipped rounds from a belt-fed automatic action at 400 RPM. The Scythe is designed as a squad-level destructive weapon — each round carries enough explosive filler to breach light walls and each burst leaves a path of destruction that Carrion's marketing materials describe as 'cultivated denial.'

The CDW-20 is mounted on a two-wheeled cart that a single operator can drag into position, deploying the weapon on its integral bipod in under 30 seconds. The cart carries 400 rounds of linked ammunition and a blast shield that protects the operator from incoming fire — though not from the weapon's own considerable backblast.

Carrion designed the Reaper for offensive suppression — not merely pinning an enemy behind cover, but systematically destroying the cover itself. A 5-second burst from the CDW-20 can demolish a concrete barricade, collapse a sandbagged position, or reduce a ground-floor room to rubble.
legality: Military restricted — heavy automatic weapons authorization
specifications: caliber: 15mm explosive-tipped effective_range: 100-1,000 meters rate_of_fire: 400 rounds per minute capacity: 400-round linked belt on cart weight: 28 kg weapon, 85 kg cart with ammunition power_source: None — conventional chemical propellant
tactical_use: The Reaper is deployed to systematically dismantle defensive positions that lighter weapons cannot defeat. Operators engage fortified positions with sustained bursts that first destroy cover, then the defenders behind it. The weapon's explosive rounds produce secondary fragmentation from the cover material itself — concrete spall, glass fragments, and structural debris become additional projectiles. In the hands of a skilled operator, the CDW-20 turns an enemy's fortification into a weapon against them.
cultural_context: Carrion Defense Works embraces their reputation as manufacturers of weapons that exist on the threshold between military and atrocity. The Reaper embodies this ethos — a weapon designed not just to kill, but to destroy the environment around the target. In GLMZ's post-engagement damage assessments, CDW-20 fire patterns are easily identified by the systematic structural destruction they leave behind. Humanitarian observers call it 'calculated ruin.'
story_hooks: A Reaper was used to demolish a community center in the lower tiers during what was supposed to be a targeted engagement against a single individual inside. The building was reduced to rubble. The target survived — they were not in the building at the time.
Carrion has received a massive order for CDW-20 systems from an anonymous buyer. The quantity — 200 units — suggests someone is arming for a war larger than any recent corporate dispute.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist heavy support weapon mounted on a two-wheeled tactical cart. The gun itself is a long-barreled automatic cannon with a distinctly aggressive profile — wide receiver housing, prominent ammunition feed mechanism running along the top, and a heavily braced bipod that extends downward like mantis legs. The entire assembly reads as industrial-grade destructive engineering: form follows function with no concessions to aesthetics.
physical_description.dimensions: Weapon body: 156 cm long, 18 cm wide at receiver, 22 cm tall. Barrel: 92 cm. Cart: 110 cm long, 75 cm wide, 105 cm tall when bipod deployed. Overall footprint when ready: approximately 140 cm × 95 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and deliberately grounded. The 28 kg weapon feels like controlled mass in its mount, while the 85 kg cart (with ammunition) requires genuine physical effort to position but sits stable once deployed. The weight distribution is purposeful — designed to anchor the operator against the weapon's violent recoil impulse.
physical_description.primary_material: Forged steel receiver and barrel. Polymer composite cart chassis and ammunition hopper. Reinforced titanium alloy for the bipod struts. Integral blast shield is welded steel plate.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with tactical flat black polymer surfaces. Steel components show intentional weathering — the finish is durable but utilitarian, without any shine. The barrel exhibits characteristic heat-staining in concentric rings, suggesting sustained fire use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal gray and tactical black. Accents: worn brass (cartridge case ejection pattern visible on shield), faded danger-red warning striping on the ammunition cart's front edge and bipod deployment bars.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip panels with aggressive texturing to prevent slippage during recoil management. The ammunition feed handle is textured knurled steel. Spade grips behind the receiver for traverse control are wrapped in weathered neoprene.
distinctive_features: Prominent twin-loop ammunition feed mechanism running the length of the receiver
Integral blast deflector shield (welded steel plate, 8mm thick) mounted perpendicular behind the receiver
Dual-axis recoil compensation system visible as heavy spring housings on either side of the barrel mount
Ammunition counter drum on the right side — mechanical rotary dial showing remaining rounds
Heat vents punched in geometric patterns along the receiver sides (functional cooling grates)
Muzzle brake with distinctive multi-port design creating a cross-shaped muzzle profile
Quick-release ammunition cart coupling with redundant safety pins
Scoring marks and impact scars on the blast shield indicating field use
Ejection port positioned with a brass deflector to direct spent casings downward
Faint engraved serial number on the left receiver plate
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS logo stamped in relief on both sides of the receiver (stylized crow/carrion bird symbol). Model designation 'CDW-20' engraved in clean sans-serif lettering on the top dust cover. Serial number on left receiver plate. Ammunition cart bears stenciled 'REAPER' designation and Carrion's corporate symbol on the shield face.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. The weapon shows evidence of heavy use — scoring on the shield, heat-discoloration on the barrel, wear patterns on grip surfaces — but zero rust or neglect. The ammunition feed mechanism is clean, bipod joints are lubricated, and the cart wheels show tread wear consistent with active deployment. This is a working weapon that is properly cared for by crews who understand what happens when a 15mm support gun malfunctions.
